plan.title: Liver drug treatment vs control DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: This is a 3-vs-3 unpaired bulk RNA-seq design in human liver tissue, raw integer STAR/featureCounts gene-level counts (12000 genes x 6 samples), single batch, comparing drug-treated vs control. The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 procedure end to end: QC of sample structure first (to catch a mislabeled or outlier sample before any test commits to it), a minimal count filter, DESeq2's built-in median-of-ratios normalization inside the negative-binomial model (no pre-normalization of the raw counts), a Wald test with an explicit control-as-reference contrast, apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold change, BH-adjusted significance at padj<0.05 with independent filtering, then fgsea preranked enrichment (Hallmark, followed by Reactome) on the Wald statistic. Because each group has only 3 replicates, the differential-expression step and the final report explicitly carry the low-power caveat: a gene absent from the significant list is not evidence of no effect, and the analysis will only be well powered for large-effect changes. A final report step consolidates DE results, fit diagnostics, enrichment results, and the reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene-set collection version).

keep genes with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
DE + enrichment report with diagnostics, power caveat, reproducibility record
